recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed unless the work group makes a new decision to reintroduce an EPUB/FHIR Book artifact with a maintained, conformant generation process.
issue_request: FHIR-8613 was a Published FHIR-core documentation issue with Persuasive with Modification resolution. It asked for the downloads page FHIR Book EPUB link to be changed from unreadable fhir-v0.0.82.epub to a readable GitHub-hosted fhir-v0.5.0.epub, but the final resolution instead withdrew the EPUB version because conformant EPUB output was not practical.
initial_application: The issue was applied in Subversion revision 6712, imported as git commit ac5f9b4d98e50aa779bfc1454fdb8cdd0db0bf91, whose message explicitly says '#8613 - abandon attempts to make the epub work' and comments out the FHIR Book EPUB row in source/downloads.html. Later downloads-page refactors removed that commented row entirely.
additional_context: source/downloads.html is still an active build page through source/hierarchy.xml. Current source/downloads.html contains current specification and package downloads and no FHIR Book, EPUB, fhir-v0.0.82.epub, or fhir-v0.5.0 EPUB link. Earlier related EPUB issues FHIR-3140 and FHIR-3792 document reader/link problems, but FHIR-8613 is the later withdrawal decision. Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Restoring or replacing the EPUB link would contradict the final FHIR-8613 resolution because the accepted outcome was withdrawal of the EPUB artifact.

related_jiras.note: Earlier Published issue added Linux EPUB-reader guidance for the old FHIR Book downloads row, which became obsolete once FHIR-8613 withdrew the EPUB artifact.
Earlier Published issue recorded that the DSTU1 FHIR ebook was corrupt or invalid, supporting the same EPUB quality problem later closed by FHIR-8613 withdrawal.
